newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely changed and very quiet.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely changed and very quiet.

text.p: Precious metal prices sat within cents of their Monday closing levels on Tuesday morning as dealers completed pre-Christmas position squaring.
After Tuesday's silver fixing, the London bullion market effectively closes until Friday December 27.
There will be no afternoon gold, platinum or palladium fixes on December 24.
Gold was fixed at $368.90 per ounce after $368.75 on Monday afternoon and a close of $368.60/$369.10.
Neither New York or the Far East where Japan returned after a national holiday on Monday moved more than fractionally.
"People are happy enough to square the book off and start again on Friday. You wouldn't want to be exposed when New York is trading on Boxing Day (December 26)," a dealer said.
A return to the market by funds and fabricators was not expected until January, the dealer added.
Silver was a cent up from its close at $4.83/$4.85 and platinum and palladium were up 25 cents at $372.00/$373.00 and unchanged at $117.00/$118.00 respectively, all in virtually tradeless markets.
